findings.title: A failed 'Add entry' wipes the text the user typed
findings.where: Plant detail page /plants/:id, New entry form (pages/plants/[id].vue addEntry)
findings.steps: Open a plant, type a journal entry, then make the POST /api/journal fail (API down, network error, session expired, plant deleted in another tab giving 404, or any 4xx/5xx). Click 'Add entry'.
findings.expected: The error is shown and the typed text stays in the textarea so the user can try again.
findings.actual: addEntry calls entryForm.reset() in its `finally` block, so the textarea is cleared on failure as well as on success. The error message appears next to an empty form and the text is lost.
findings.evidence: Code: `finally { addingEntry.value = false; entryForm.value?.reset(); entryForm.value?.focus() }`. The reset() doc comment even says 'Clears the text after a successful save'.

findings.title: Journal page error state has no retry
findings.steps: Open /journal while the API is failing or unreachable.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that reloads the list once the server is back.
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown. There is no retry control, so the user has to edit the search text or reload the page.
findings.evidence: pages/journal.vue renders `<AlertMessage v-if="loadError">` with no button and never calls refresh.

findings.title: Journal section on plant detail has no retry when loading fails
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal?plant_id=… fail while the plant itself loads.
findings.actual: Shows 'Could not load the journal.' with no retry, and no list or empty state. refreshJournal only runs after an add or delete.
findings.evidence: journalLoadError alert in [id].vue has no action.

findings.title: Search longer than 80 characters gives a raw validation error
findings.steps: Type or paste more than 80 characters into the Journal search box.
findings.expected: The input is limited to 80 characters or explains the limit in plain words.
findings.actual: The server returns 422 and the page shows 'Q: String should have at most 80 characters' in place of results. The input has no maxlength.
findings.evidence: curl /api/journal?q=<81 a's> -> 422 string_too_long. The input in journal.vue has no maxlength.

findings.title: Out-of-range integer ids return 500 instead of 4xx
findings.steps: curl -X DELETE /api/journal/99999999999999999999 (or the same for PUT, ?plant_id=, or plant_id in the POST body).
findings.evidence: All four requests returned 'Internal Server Error 500'.

findings.title: Retry after a timeout or lost response creates duplicate entries; repeat delete shows an error
findings.steps: Add an entry while the response is lost or slow, then click Add again. Or retry a delete whose first request went through.
findings.expected: One entry is created, and a repeat delete is treated as success.
findings.actual: POST has no idempotency key, so each retry inserts a new row. A second DELETE returns 404 'Journal entry not found.', which is shown as an error. Requests also have no 10 s timeout, so a hung request leaves 'Saving…' on screen indefinitely.
findings.evidence: A second DELETE of /api/journal/4 returned 404. The api client ($fetch.create) sets no timeout and the request sends no idempotency key.

findings.title: Journal accepts absurd dates such as year 0001
findings.steps: Pick 0001-01-01 in the date field, or POST it directly.
findings.expected: A reasonable lower bound is enforced with a clear message.
findings.actual: Accepted (201) and shown as an entry dated 1 Jan 1, which sorts last.

findings.title: Long unbroken plant names may overflow the journal feed at 375 px
findings.steps: Name a plant with a long string that has no spaces, write an entry for it, then view /journal at 375 px wide.
findings.actual: .journal-feed__plant has no overflow-wrap (only the entry body does), so the link can cause sideways scrolling.
findings.evidence: The CSS diff sets overflow-wrap:anywhere only on .journal-entry__body.
